hypothesis: Adding dewpoint depression, 3-hour pressure trend, and gust-minus-mean wind as explicit input features will give the model direct physical precursors for fog/haze formation and frontal/turbulence transitions, improving rare-class hazard detection and long-horizon forecast stability.
evidence_anchor: Failure slice (d): hazard-class F1 fluctuates 0.53-0.79 across seeds and val support is extremely sparse; fog/haze is a known minority class where temperature-moisture coupling (T-Td) and pressure tendency are textbook precursors, yet the current representation forces the model to infer these indirectly from raw channels.
expected_effect: Increase fog_haze_f1 by at least +0.05 absolute over scratch baseline; reduce T+8 RMSE by at least 0.002 (relative improvement ~4%) by providing stabilizing physical context.
falsification: On the visible validation endpoint grid, if the mean fog_haze_f1 across seeds does not improve by >=0.05 over the scratch baseline, or if T+8 RMSE degrades by more than 0.001, the hypothesis is refuted.
patch_plan: In aerowf_downstream_v2/src/trial_features.py, modify build_forecast_inputs to compute and append dewpoint_depression (T - Td), pressure_trend_3h (difference between latest and 3h-prior pressure), and gust_minus_mean (gust - sustained wind) from available METAR fields. Keep existing channels unchanged; add these as extra numeric features. Ensure the feature ordering is consistent and update any internal normalization to handle the new channels. No changes to target generation or model architecture.
